literal: When the bath was done and they were about to lay him out, the corpse was small, shrunk to only about three chi.
idiomatic: When the bath was done and they were about to lay him out, the corpse had shrunk to barely three chi.

literal: Wenxuan ordered the coffin opened and looked — an empty coffin only.
idiomatic: Gao Yang ordered the coffin opened and looked inside — only an empty coffin.

literal: Fahe had written on the wall of his dwelling and plastered it over; when the plaster fell away, text read: "Ten years as Son of Heaven would still be tolerable; a hundred days as Son of Heaven burns like fire; a full year as Son of Heaven — thrones pass in turn.
idiomatic: Lu Fahe had written on the wall of his chamber and plastered it over; when the plaster fell away, text read, "Ten years as Son of Heaven would still be tolerable; a hundred days as Son of Heaven burns like fire; a full year as Son of Heaven — thrones pass in turn.

literal: " It also said: "One mother bears three Sons of Heaven; two heavens together span five years.
idiomatic: " It also said, "One mother bears three Sons of Heaven; two heavens together span five years.

literal: " Interpreters held that Empress Dowager Lou bore three sons who became sovereign; from Xiaozhao's accession until Wucheng passed the throne to the Later Ruler was five years in all.
idiomatic: " Interpreters held that Empress Dowager Lou bore three sons who became sovereign — from Emperor Xiaozhao's accession until Wucheng passed the throne to the Later Ruler, five years in all.

literal: While Fahe was in Jing and Ying he had a young concubine, aged about twenty-odd, who called herself the Yue crone; she wore monastic garb, would not marry, and constantly followed Fahe east and west.
idiomatic: While Lu Fahe was in Jing and Ying he had a young concubine of about twenty who called herself the Yue crone. She wore monastic garb, would not marry, and constantly followed him wherever he went.

literal: Some privately coupled with her for more than ten years.
idiomatic: Some had privately coupled with her for more than ten years.

literal: Now she was cast off and took other lovers.
idiomatic: Now she was cast off and took other lovers.

literal: The authorities investigated; all proved true.
idiomatic: The authorities investigated; all proved true.

literal: The Yue crone then married again and bore several sons.
idiomatic: The Yue crone then married again and bore several sons.

literal: Wang Lin, styled Ziheng, was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
idiomatic: Wang Lin, styled Ziheng, was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.

literal: His father Xiansi was regular attendant in the kingdom of Prince of Xiangdong of Liang.
idiomatic: His father Xiansi had been regular attendant in the kingdom of Liang's Prince of Xiangdong.

literal: Lin came from a military family; when Emperor Yuan held his princely fief, Lin's sisters all entered the inner quarters and won favor — Lin thereby, before his cap was full, gained a place at the prince's side.
idiomatic: Lin came from a military family. When Emperor Yuan of Liang still held his princely fief, Lin's sisters all entered the inner quarters and won favor; Lin thereby gained a place at the prince's side before he had even capped.

literal: In youth he loved martial affairs and thus became a commander.
idiomatic: In youth he loved martial affairs and thus became a commander.

literal: In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing crossed the Yangzi; Lin was sent to present ten thousand piculs of grain.
idiomatic: In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing crossed the Yangzi; Lin was sent to present ten thousand piculs of grain.

literal: Before he arrived the capital fell; he sank the grain mid-river and returned by light boat to Jingzhou.
idiomatic: Before he arrived the capital fell. He sank the grain mid-river and returned by light boat to Jingzhou.

literal: He was gradually promoted to Administrator of Yueyang and, for military merit, enfeoffed Marquis of Jianning.
idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to administrator of Yueyang and, for military merit, enfeoffed Marquis of Jianning.

literal: Hou Jing sent General Song Zixian to hold Yingzhou; Lin attacked and took it, capturing Zixian.
idiomatic: Hou Jing sent General Song Zixian to hold Yingzhou; Lin attacked and took it, capturing Zixian.

literal: He also followed Wang Sengbian in defeating Jing.
idiomatic: He also followed Wang Sengbian in defeating Hou Jing.

literal: Later he was made Governor of Xiangzhou.
idiomatic: Later he was made governor of Xiangzhou.

literal: Lin was fierce and surpassing among men, yet could humble himself before soldiers; rewards he received he did not bring home.
idiomatic: Lin was fierce beyond ordinary men, yet could humble himself before his troops; whatever rewards he received he did not bring home.

literal: Under his command were ten thousand men, mostly river-and-Huai bandits.
idiomatic: Under his command were ten thousand men, mostly bandits of the Jiang and Huai.

literal: In merit for pacifying Jing he ranked first with Du Kan; relying on favor he ran riot in Jiankang.
idiomatic: In merit for pacifying Jing he ranked first with Du Kan; relying on favor he ran riot in Jiankang.

literal: Wang Sengbian forbade it but could not; fearing he would stir rebellion, he memorialized asking execution.
idiomatic: Wang Sengbian forbade it but could not; fearing Lin would stir rebellion, he memorialized asking that he be executed.

literal: Lin also suspected disaster; he ordered Chief Clerk Lu Na to lead his troops ahead to Xiangzhou while he himself went straight up to Jiangling.
idiomatic: Lin also suspected disaster. He ordered chief clerk Lu Na to lead his troops ahead to Xiangzhou while he himself went straight up to Jiangling.

literal: About to depart, he said to Na and the rest: "If I do not return, where will you go?
idiomatic: About to depart, he said to Na and the rest, "If I do not return, where will you go?

literal: " All said: "We ask only to die in your service.
idiomatic: " All said, "We ask only to die in your service.

literal: " They wept and parted.
idiomatic: " They wept and parted.

literal: When he arrived, the emperor had him sent down to the law; but Court Gentleman of the Imperial Law Huang Luohan and Minister of the Grand Treasury Zhang Zai went to announce the decree to Lin's army.
idiomatic: When he arrived, the emperor had him sent down to the law; but court gentleman of the imperial law Huang Luohan and minister of the grand treasury Zhang Zai went to announce the decree to Lin's army.

literal: Lu Na and the soldiers all wept facing the envoys and would not accept orders; they reported to Huang Luohan and killed Zhang Zai.
idiomatic: Lu Na and the soldiers all wept facing the envoys and would not accept orders; they reported to Huang Luohan and killed Zhang Zai.

literal: Zai was harsh by nature, trusted by the emperor; Jingzhou hated him like an enemy — so Na and the rest, playing on men's desires, drew out his entrails and tied them to a horse's leg, making the horse run until the guts were gone and breath ended; then they carved him piecemeal through the five punishments and beheaded him.
idiomatic: Zai was harsh by nature and trusted by the emperor; Jingzhou hated him like an enemy. So Na and the rest, playing on men's desires, drew out his entrails and tied them to a horse's leg, making the horse run until the guts were gone and breath ended; then they carved him piecemeal through the five punishments and beheaded him.

literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang sent Wang Sengbian to attack Na; Na and the rest were defeated and fled to Changsha.
idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang sent Wang Sengbian to attack Na; Na and the rest were defeated and fled to Changsha.

literal: At that time Xiangzhou was not yet pacified, and the Prince of Wuling's troops were very strong; public and private in Jiangling were afraid, and men harbored other schemes.
idiomatic: At that time Xiangzhou was not yet pacified, and the Prince of Wuling's troops were very strong; public and private in Jiangling were afraid, and men harbored other schemes.

literal: Na memorialized stating Lin's crimes, asking restoration to his original post, willing to be slaves forever.
idiomatic: Na memorialized stating Lin's crimes, asking that he be restored to his original post and offering that they would be slaves forever.

literal: Emperor Yuan then shackled Lin and sent him to Changsha.
idiomatic: Emperor Yuan then shackled Lin and sent him to Changsha.

literal: At the time Na's troops were out fighting; when Lin arrived, Sengbian mounted the tower chariots to show him.
idiomatic: At the time Na's troops were out fighting; when Lin arrived, Sengbian mounted the tower chariots to show him.

literal: Na and the rest cast down their weapons and bowed together; the whole army wept and said: "We beg Prince Lin enter the city — we will come out at once.
idiomatic: Na and the rest cast down their weapons and bowed together; the whole army wept and said, "We beg Prince Lin enter the city — we will come out at once.

literal: " When Lin was released and entered, Na and the rest then surrendered, and Xiangzhou was pacified.
idiomatic: " When Lin was released and entered, Na and the rest then surrendered, and Xiangzhou was pacified.

literal: Lin was restored to his post and ordered to resist Xiao Ji.
idiomatic: Lin was restored to his post and ordered to resist Xiao Ji.

literal: When Ji was pacified, Lin was made Governor of Hengzhou.
idiomatic: When Ji was pacified, Lin was made governor of Hengzhou.

literal: Emperor Yuan was much given to suspicion; because Lin's following was very large and he had won men's hearts, he was sent out beyond the ranges; he also received the post of Area Commander and Governor of Guangzhou.
idiomatic: Emperor Yuan was much given to suspicion. Because Lin's following was very large and he had won men's hearts, he was sent out beyond the ranges; he also received the post of area commander and governor of Guangzhou.

literal: His friend Master of Documents Li Ying, whom the emperor favored — Lin told him: "Lin has received your pull and lift; I have always wished to give my life to repay the state's grace.
idiomatic: His friend master of documents Li Ying, whom the emperor favored — Lin told him, "Lin has received your pull and lift; I have always wished to give my life to repay the state's grace.

literal: The realm is not yet settled; moving Lin beyond the ranges — if there should be the slightest mishap, how could you use Lin's strength?
idiomatic: The realm is not yet settled; moving Lin beyond the ranges — if there should be the slightest mishap, how could you use Lin's strength?

literal: I reckon Your Majesty now only suspects Lin.
idiomatic: I reckon Your Majesty now only suspects Lin.

literal: Lin's share of ambition is limited — could I contend with Your Majesty to be emperor?
idiomatic: Lin's share of ambition is limited — could I contend with Your Majesty to be emperor?

literal: Why not make Lin Governor of Yongzhou, to garrison Wuning? Lin himself would release troops to farm the fields and guard the state on your behalf.
idiomatic: Why not make Lin governor of Yongzhou, to garrison Wuning? Lin himself would release troops to farm the fields and guard the state on your behalf.

literal: If alarm comes, movements would be known to each other.
idiomatic: If alarm comes, movements would be known to each other.

literal: How does that compare with casting one far off in Lingnan, ten thousand li apart — if in a day something changes, what then?
idiomatic: How does that compare with casting one far off in Lingnan, ten thousand li apart — if in a day something changes, what then?

literal: Lin does not wish to sit long in southern Jing; it is only that the state's plan is thus.
idiomatic: Lin does not wish to sit long in southern Jing; it is only that the state's plan is thus.

literal: " Ying agreed with his words but dared not report them; so Lin led his host to garrison Lingnan.
idiomatic: " Ying agreed with his words but dared not report them; so Lin led his host to garrison Lingnan.

literal: Emperor Yuan, pressed by Wei siege, summoned Lin to the rescue and made him Governor of Xiangzhou again.
idiomatic: Emperor Yuan, pressed by Wei siege, summoned Lin to the rescue and made him governor of Xiangzhou again.

literal: Lin's army halted at Changsha; learning Wei had taken Jiangling and set up Liang Prince Cha, he held mourning for Emperor Yuan; the whole army wore white.
idiomatic: Lin's army halted at Changsha. Learning Wei had taken Jiangling and set up Liang Prince Cha, he held mourning for Emperor Yuan; the whole army wore white.

literal: He sent a separate commander Hou Ping with a fleet to attack Liang.
idiomatic: He sent a separate commander Hou Ping with a fleet to attack Liang.

literal: Lin encamped at Changsha and issued proclamations to all quarters, planning advance.
idiomatic: Lin encamped at Changsha and issued proclamations to all quarters, planning advance.

literal: At the time Prince of Changsha Xiao Shao and the upstream commanders pushed Lin as league leader.
idiomatic: At the time Prince of Changsha Xiao Shao and the upstream commanders pushed Lin as league leader.

literal: Though Hou Ping could not cross the Yangzi, he repeatedly defeated Liang forces; yet because Lin's military prestige did not reach him, he in turn would no longer accept orders.
idiomatic: Though Hou Ping could not cross the Yangzi, he repeatedly defeated Liang forces; yet because Lin's military prestige did not reach him, he in turn would no longer accept orders.

literal: Lin sent generals to attack him but could not overcome him; his army was also old, soldiers weary, unable to advance.
idiomatic: Lin sent generals to attack him but could not overcome him; his army was also old, soldiers weary, unable to advance.

literal: He sent envoys with a memorial to Qi and also presented a tame elephant;
idiomatic: He sent envoys with a memorial to Qi and also presented a tame elephant;

literal: he also sent submission to Wei, asking for his wife and children;
idiomatic: he also sent submission to Wei, asking for his wife and children;

literal: and he also declared himself minister to Liang.
idiomatic: and he also declared himself minister to Liang.

literal: Chen Baxian had killed Wang Sengbian and raised Emperor Jing, summoning Lin as attendant and minister of works.
idiomatic: Chen Baxian had killed Wang Sengbian and raised Emperor Jing, summoning Lin as attendant and minister of works.

literal: Lin did not obey; he greatly built tower-ships, intending a righteous rising.
idiomatic: Lin did not obey; he greatly built tower-ships, intending a righteous rising.

literal: Lin's commanders each rode one vessel; whenever he moved, battle ships numbered in thousands, named "Wild Boar."
idiomatic: Lin's commanders each rode one vessel; whenever he moved, battle ships numbered in thousands, named "Wild Boar."

literal: Emperor Wu of Chen sent Generals Hou Andu and Zhou Wenyu to execute Lin, then accepted Liang's abdication.
idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Chen sent generals Hou Andu and Zhou Wenyu to execute Lin, then accepted Liang's abdication.

literal: Andu sighed: "Shall I be defeated? The army has no righteous name."
idiomatic: Andu sighed, "Shall I be defeated? The army has no righteous name."

literal: They fought upstream at Zhunkou; Lin rode a level-shouldered litter, grasped an axe and directed them, capturing Andu and Wenyu; of the rest none escaped.
idiomatic: They fought upstream at Zhunkou. Lin rode a level-shouldered litter, grasped an axe and directed them, capturing Andu and Wenyu; of the rest none escaped.

literal: Only Zhou Tiehu alone betrayed kindness — him he beheaded.
idiomatic: Only Zhou Tiehu alone betrayed kindness — him he beheaded.

literal: He shackled Andu and Wenyu aboard the vessel where Lin sat and set a eunuch to guard them.
idiomatic: He shackled Andu and Wenyu aboard the vessel where Lin sat and set a eunuch to guard them.

literal: Lin then moved the Xiangzhou military headquarters to Yingcheng, with armor on a hundred thousand, drilling troops at Baisui Ford.
idiomatic: Lin then moved the Xiangzhou military headquarters to Yingcheng, with armor on a hundred thousand, drilling troops at Baisui Ford.

literal: Lin inspected the army and said: "This can be an army to relieve the ruler — who was Wen Taizhen!
idiomatic: Lin inspected the army and said, "This can be an army to relieve the ruler — who was Wen Taizhen!

literal: " The channel lords of Jiangnan, Xiong Tanlang and Zhou Di, wavered in loyalty; Lin sent Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoxiang together to attack them.
idiomatic: " The channel lords of Jiangnan, Xiong Tanlang and Zhou Di, wavered in loyalty; Lin sent Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoxiang together to attack them.

literal: All three generals were defeated and taken prisoner by the enemy.
idiomatic: All three generals were defeated and taken prisoner by the enemy.

literal: Andu, Wenyu, and the rest all escaped back to Jiankang.
idiomatic: Andu, Wenyu, and the rest all escaped back to Jiankang.

literal: Earlier, when Wei took Jiangling, Prince Zhuang of Yongjia was only seven; he hid in a household; later Lin welcomed him back to Xiang and escorted him east.
idiomatic: Earlier, when Wei took Jiangling, Prince Zhuang of Yongjia was only seven; he hid in a household; later Lin welcomed him back to Xiang and escorted him east.

literal: When Emperor Jing was enthroned, Zhuang was sent as hostage to Qi, asking that Zhuang be received as ruler of Liang.
idiomatic: When Emperor Jing was enthroned, Zhuang was sent as hostage to Qi, asking that Zhuang be received as ruler of Liang.

literal: Wenxuan sent troops to escort him and also dispatched Concurrent Secretariat Supervisor Li Piaomo to invest Lin as Liang Chancellor, Commander of All Armies Within and Without, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Gao Yang sent troops to escort him and also dispatched concurrent secretariat supervisor Li Piaomo to invest Lin as Liang chancellor, commander of all armies within and without, and recorder of the masters of writing.

literal: Attendant Yang Yin and You Quanzhi and others carried imperial writs to proclaim favors in the Jiang region; from Lin downward all received gifts.
idiomatic: Attendant Yang Yin and You Quanzhi and others carried imperial writs to proclaim favors in the Jiang region; from Lin downward all received gifts.

literal: Lin sent his nephew's son Shubao to lead sons of the ten provincial governors' families to Ye, to install Zhuang in Liang's mandate at Yingzhou.
idiomatic: Lin sent his nephew's son Shubao to lead sons of the ten provincial governors' families to Ye, to install Zhuang in Liang's mandate at Yingzhou.

literal: Zhuang made Lin attendant, bearer of credentials, grand general, and director of the secretariat, changed his enfeoffment to Duke of Ancheng, and the rest followed Qi's earlier orders.
idiomatic: Zhuang made Lin attendant, bearer of credentials, grand general, and director of the secretariat, changed his enfeoffment to Duke of Ancheng, and the rest followed Qi's earlier orders.

literal: When Chen Baxian took the throne, Lin then supported Zhuang encamped at Ruxukou.
idiomatic: When Chen Baxian took the throne, Lin then supported Zhuang encamped at Ruxukou.

literal: Qi sent Acting Governor of Yangzhou Route Murong Yan with troops to the river as his rear support.
idiomatic: Qi sent acting governor of the Yangzhou route Murong Yan with troops to the river as his rear support.

literal: Chen sent Wu Mingche, inspector of Anzhou, up the Yangzi by night, intending a surprise on Tuncheng.
idiomatic: Chen sent Wu Mingche, inspector of Anzhou, up the Yangzi by night, intending a surprise on Tuncheng.

literal: Lin sent Ren Zhong, Administrator of Baling, who inflicted a great defeat; Mingche barely escaped with his life.
idiomatic: Lin sent Ren Zhong, administrator of Baling, who inflicted a great defeat; Mingche barely escaped with his life.

literal: Lin's troops then went downstream; Chen sent Minister of Works Hou Andu and others to resist.
idiomatic: Lin's troops then went downstream; Chen sent minister of works Hou Andu and others to resist.

literal: Hou Tian and the rest, seeing Lin's army at its height, drew off into Wuhu to avoid it.
idiomatic: Hou Tian and the rest, seeing Lin's army at its height, drew off into Wuhu to avoid it.

literal: Suddenly a southwest wind arose; Lin thought heaven favored him and would drive straight on Yangzhou.
idiomatic: Suddenly a southwest wind arose; Lin thought heaven favored him and would drive straight on Yangzhou.

literal: Hou Tian and the rest slowly emerged from Wuhu and followed his rear.
idiomatic: Hou Tian and the rest slowly emerged from Wuhu and followed his rear.

literal: By the time battle joined, the southwest wind had turned to Tian's use.
idiomatic: By the time battle joined, the southwest wind had turned to Tian's use.

literal: Lin's men cast fire beacons at the enemy ships — all burned their own ships instead.
idiomatic: Lin's men cast fire beacons at the enemy ships — all burned their own ships instead.

literal: Lin's fleet broke in disorder; a tenth or two of the soldiers drowned; the rest all abandoned ship for shore and were killed by Chen forces almost to the last man.
idiomatic: Lin's fleet broke in disorder; a tenth or two of the soldiers drowned; the rest all abandoned ship for shore and were killed by Chen forces almost to the last man.

literal: Earlier Lin had ordered Left Chief Clerk Yuan Mi and Imperial Censor Liu Zhongwei jointly to command troops guarding Zhuang; when the army fell, Mi surrendered to Chen, and Zhongwei took Zhuang to Liyang.
idiomatic: Earlier Lin had ordered left chief clerk Yuan Mi and imperial censor Liu Zhongwei jointly to command troops guarding Zhuang; when the army fell, Mi surrendered to Chen, and Zhongwei took Zhuang to Liyang.

literal: Soon Lin and Zhuang surrendered together at the capital of Ye.
idiomatic: Soon Lin and Zhuang surrendered together at the capital of Ye.

literal: Emperor Xiaozhao sent Lin out from Hefei to muster old adherents and plan advance again.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhao sent Lin out from Hefei to muster old adherents and plan advance again.

literal: Lin repaired ships and sent parties to recruit; the porters and Chu of Huainan all wished to give their strength.
idiomatic: Lin repaired ships and sent parties to recruit; the porters and Chu of Huainan all wished to give their strength.

literal: Chen's Inspector of Hezhou Pei Jinghui was son-in-law to Lin's elder brother Min; he asked to guide the Qi army with his private followers.
idiomatic: Chen's inspector of Hezhou Pei Jinghui was son-in-law to Lin's elder brother Min; he asked to guide the Qi army with his private followers.

literal: Xiaozhao entrusted Lin with Commissioner Left Assistant Director Lu Qian to lead troops to answer the call, but hesitated undecided.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhao entrusted Lin with commissioner left assistant director Lu Qian to lead troops to answer the call, but hesitated undecided.

literal: Jinghui feared the affair would leak; he threw himself on Qi.
idiomatic: Jinghui feared the affair would leak; he threw himself on Qi.

literal: Xiaozhao granted Lin an imperial letter, ordering him to garrison Shouyang; his subordinate commanders might all go with him. Lin was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Bearer of Equal Hall with the Three Dukes, Governor of Yangzhou, enfeoffed Duke of Kuaiji; arms were increased, and drums and pipes were also given.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhao granted Lin an imperial letter, ordering him to garrison Shouyang; his subordinate commanders might all go with him. Lin was made grand general of agile cavalry, bearer of equal hall with the three dukes, governor of Yangzhou, enfeoffed Duke of Kuaiji; arms were increased, and drums and pipes were also given.

literal: Lin made strict readiness by land and water, waiting to move on opportunity.
idiomatic: Lin made strict readiness by land and water, waiting to move on opportunity.

literal: Just then Chen and Qi made peace; Lin was made to wait for later plans.
idiomatic: Just then Chen and Qi made peace; Lin was made to wait for later plans.
